title: Tokenflow p95-drift harness for multi-tenant throughput resilience
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a repeatable, configurable load harness that measures token-level throughput (tokens/sec) and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) while exercising continuous batching + queueing under realistic mixed-tenant workloads. The goal is to detect regressions in p95 and tokens/sec that arise from changes to scheduler heuristics, batching thresholds, KV cache behavior, or kernel selection. This ticket covers design, implementation, CI integration, and an initial baselining run for current master.
steps: Design arrival-pattern library: Poisson baseline, burst windows (hot-starts), long-tail sessions, and diurnal mixes to emulate multi-tenant traffic.
Implement traffic generator that can synthesize multi-tenant requests with configurable sequence length distributions, model variants (fp16, int8/quantized), and KV cache locality parameters.
Wire generator to runtime test harness to collect per-request metrics: queue_time_ms, batch_size_at_dispatch, tokens_generated, model_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, gpu_util_pct.
Add aggregation pipelines that compute tokens/sec per-second, rolling p50/p95/p99, batch size histograms, and queue depth heatmaps. Persist outputs to JSON + Prometheus metrics for dashboarding.

Create regression detection rules: compute baseline windows and detect >10% tokens/sec drop or >20% absolute p95 increase for 5-minute sustained periods, trigger alert and auto-open ENG ticket with the run snapshot.

Run initial experiments across three workload mixes: (A) latency-sensitive low-QPS short sequences, (B) throughput-sensitive sustained mid-QPS medium sequences, (C) mixed multi-tenant blend with correlated bursts. Save all artifacts.
Add CI job (nightly) that runs a lightweight subset and fails if regression rules trip; store full runs in S3 for on-demand analysis.
Document harness and create dashboard in Console (per-route p95, tokens/sec, batch distribution, queue time) with links from the ticket.
Share results with scheduler and kernels teams and iterate on mitigation strategies (priority preemption, dynamic batching thresholds, cache warmup).
acceptance_criteria: Traffic generator supports at least 4 arrival profiles and tenant mixing parameters.
Collected metrics include tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, batch size histogram, queue_time_ms, and kv_cache_hit_rate for every run.
Regression detection rules are implemented and validated against synthetic regressions (introduce a 15% added queue delay and verify an alert).
A baseline run for current master exists (artifact URL in comments) and nightly CI job is configured to run subset tests.
Run artifacts are queryable and a Console dashboard prototype is available with per-route views and time-series for p95 and tokens/sec.
Hand-off notes and follow-up actions are documented and triaged with scheduler and kernels owners.

notes: Trade-offs: heavier fidelity (full GPU-backed runs) gives realistic measurements but is costly; plan is to keep nightly subset on smaller instances and run full-fidelity suites on-demand. Regression thresholds are intentionally conservative to balance noise vs signal; tuning will happen after first 2 weeks of baseline data.
